explanation:
I found no other declaration stating that the coercion of `p ⊔ p'` for submodules equals the pointwise sum of the two sets. I searched `Submodule.coe_sup`, `sup_coe`, `add_eq_sup`, `mem_sup'`, and the Submodule, Span and Module directories for coercion-of-sup lemmas.

- **`Submodule.add_eq_sup`** (`Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Pointwise.lean`) only says `p + q = p ⊔ q` for the pointwise addition on `Submodule`. That is not the set-level statement.
- **`HomogeneousIdeal.coe_sup`** and **`FractionalIdeal.coeIdeal_sup`** concern different types.
- **`ClosedSubmodule.coe_sup`** (`Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ClosedSubmodule.lean`) is about closed submodules, and I did not read its statement.
- I did not check whether `AddSubmonoid` has an analogous lemma. Even if it does, it is stated for a different type, so deriving this theorem from it would need extra work.
